title: Telemetry Lexicon: Per-Model & Per-Route Chronicle View Prototype
creator: Claire Zhang
description: A compact, scannable console surface that unifies per-model and per-route telemetry into a single chronicle-style view. This prototype explores a hybrid layout combining a focused microtrace timeline with an adaptive metric panel (latency percentiles, throughput, token flow), plus a cost overlay and rollout status strip. The goal is to make root-cause and cost-impact diagnosis fast for engineers and product owners without leaving the Console.
goals: Surface p50/p95/p99 latency intuition and outliers quickly
Expose token-level breakdowns (input/prefix/generated) and per-request token waterfall
Enable rapid comparison between model versions and routes (A/B/canary) with baseline shading
Provide a lightweight cost overlay to link token usage to estimated spend
Keep the view dense but legible on 1280px widths; support expansion to a full canvas
success_criteria: Engineers can identify a latency anomaly and its top 2 likely causes within 3 clicks
PMs can compare two model versions' token-efficiency delta over a 24h window
Prototype usability test median task time under 90s for common diag tasks
Design integrates with rollouts strip so canary failures are discoverable from the same surface
design_notes: Primary layout: left column 'chronicle' microtrace list (compact rows) + right column metric canvas
Metric canvas top row: latency sparkline with percentile bands (p50/p95/p99), hover drill shows distribution violin for the selected time slice
Throughput: stacked bar of successful vs throttled requests with RPS trendline overlaid
Token flow: progressive waterfall per-request aggregated histogram + 'token-sankey' mini to show prefix vs generation ratio
Cost overlay: toggle on/off; when enabled shows semi-transparent cost heatmap over sparkline and estimated $/1k tokens metric
Rollouts integration: horizontal strip above chronicle showing active rollouts, can click to filter chronicle to canary vs stable traffic
Comparison mode: select two snapshots (versions/routes) to render difference ribbons; uses neutral gray baseline to avoid color bias
Responsive behavior: at <=1100px collapse microtrace list into an accordion, primary metric canvas remains visible; charts switch to simplified 'spark' mode
Interactions: brush to zoom, click percentile band to open sample request list, hover token-sankey to highlight contributing prompts
Accessibility: color choices meet 4.5:1 for primary contrast; provide keyboard affordances for time-range and compare actions
Performance: render only visible microtraces; lazy-load heavy violin and sankey visualizations on demand
chart_specs: Latency sparkline: multi-series line showing p50 (solid), p95 (dashed), p99 (dot); percentile band shading between p50-p95 and p95-p99; Y-axis linear ms; sampling interval 1m or derived based on range
Latency distribution: violin plot for selected slice with median marker and jittered sample points; tooltip shows mean, stddev, count
Throughput: stacked bar by result type (200/4xx/5xx/throttled) with RPS line (secondary axis); hover shows absolute counts
Token waterfall: stacked area histogram showing input/prefix/generated tokens aggregated per minute; measure toggles between tokens and cost-estimate
Microtrace swimlane: each row shows request duration as a horizontal bar scaled to chart width; color by latency bucket (green/yellow/red), click opens request-level trace
Baseline ribbons: in comparison mode render diff as green/red area between the two selected series; allow absolute and relative toggles
reviewers_feedback: PM (J. Patel): +1 on combining cost overlay but request estimate variance note - add guidance on currency/region assumptions
Eng (M. Solano): Likes lazy-load approach; asks for explicit metrics about payload size before enabling violin/sankey
Data (R. Gupta): Recommend adding a 'sample size' indicator when percentiles are shown to avoid overinterpreting p99 in low-volume slices
Design (L. Moreno): Suggest tighter spacing for microtrace rows and an optional 'compact mode' switch
Security (S. O'Neill): Flagged that token-level sampling must be redacted for PII before surfacing in the microtrace tooltip
decisions: Keep cost overlay opt-in and clearly labeled; base estimates on USD by default with a tooltip for currency context
Implement sample-size badge on percentile charts (low/medium/high) and gray out p99 when sample < 50
Expose a 'redaction filter' in settings to enforce PII stripping on microtrace payloads; default set to enabled
Prioritize lazy-loading of heavy visualizations in the next sprint (ENG-12021) to meet console performance SLOs
